answer: Sybil weight is capped by outside revenue, not stake. A vote equals fees from payers outside the cluster: a payer counts only if its income, traced three hops back, ends at independent customers. A farm can shuffle tokens across a thousand keys, but they form a closed spiral and earn zero. Real weight needs a plume of genuine demand: strangers paying for good work. Faking it means building real customers or buying receipts at market price, which is finite. Each identity must carry its own customers, so a vote's cost never amortizes. Only ferrous, externally earned income survives the trace.
